# Test fixtures

Shared inputs for unit tests and for phases that start before real data exists.

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `map-minimal.json` | A 200 m east–west two-way road through a signalled four-way junction at x = 100, inside an R.420 built-up zone. West arm: dashed centre line, a crosswalk with a stop line before it, a P.127 50 km/h zone bound to the eastbound lane `rw-e` only (x 10 to 96.5). North arm: double solid line and a no-left-turn restriction (P.123a). South arm: one-way northbound (I.407a) with a P.102 no-entry line at its mouth. One NPC car (westbound, starts at t = 0) and one pedestrian (starts when the ego reaches x 40 to 60). Two checkpoints and a finish on the eastbound lanes. |
| `map-junction.json` | A signalled four-way junction `j1` at the origin (box ±7 m) with 150 m arms, written by hand for the traffic and fault tests. The west arm has three lanes: two eastbound (`rw-e0` the kerb lane, `rw-e1`) and one westbound; the east, north and south arms have one lane each way. One signal head per stop line, east–west (`sig-w`, `sig-e`) and north–south (`sig-n`, `sig-s`, offset 30 s) in opposed phases. 13 connectors (no U-turns) and 37 conflict zones (`cross` where paths come within 2.5 m, `merge` where they share an exit lane), a `traffic` block with a source on every inbound lane and a sink on every outbound lane and the 75% motorbike mix, a 4-storey shophouse and three props. Every signal has one far-side repeater 1.5 m past the junction box on the right of its straight-on line: a mast arm for the two-lane west approach (`sig-w`), a post for the others. Lane arrows on `rw-e0` (straight, right) and `rw-e1` (straight, left), their tips 15 m before `sl-w`, match the lanes' connectors. One 1.5 m crosswalk `cw-w` sits in the 2 m between `sl-w` and the box (narrower than a real zebra, so no stop line moves), governed by `sig-w` and timed for pedestrians by `sig-n`. No scripted actors and an empty `laneJoins` (no plain join; the contract tests add one by mutation). |
| `frames-straight.json` | 120 frames (2 s) of `car-sedan` at a constant 15 m/s (54 km/h) along `rw-e` from x = 5, generated by the frame builder (every `input` carries `pushBack: false`); scripted poses carry the traffic pose fields with the shared off lamps and empty violations. The ego enters the 50 km/h zone at tick 20; 4 km/h over is below every speeding band, so the run is clean. |
| `rule-sample.yaml` | The car speeding rule with two tiers (D6.3.a, D6.5.đ) and `paramBasis`. Danger levels and `sustainS` are sample values. |
| `clauses-sample.yaml` | The two clauses it cites, plus D6.2.a with its real ND 238 amendment. Neither speeding clause is amended by ND 238, so the amendment example uses another clause. |
| `rules-bundle.json` | A car-only `RulesBundle`: the sample rule, its clauses, five sources, two TT 38 speed defaults (`verified: false`), two sign meanings (`figureChecked: null`), the scoring table and a `collisionPolicy`. The policy also carries the fault-table keys (`faultRows`, `nonContributingRules`, `rearEndContributingRules`, `excusingViolations`, `aftermathWindowS`, `excuseMaxSpeedGainMps`, `paramBasis`, `noticeTexts`), copied from `data/scoring/collision-policy.yaml`. The policy's accident lists are copied from the ND 168 research; the accident and va chạm clause records themselves are not in this fixture. Source `issued` dates not read from the texts are `null`. |
| `maps-index.json`, `credits.json` | Two entries each. `fixture-osm` is a placeholder entry, not a real map. The CC BY entry in `credits.json` (`models/scooter.glb`) is a sample that exercises `creditLine`; that file is not shipped. The shipped credits are `data/credits/credits.json`, which the release gate reads. |
| `hud-states.json` | `ready`, `running`, `withToasts`, `paused` and `finished` HUD states. The toasts cover a verified clause, an unverified one, an inferred one (suy luận), one with design parameters (ngưỡng của trò chơi), one with an amendment, and a score-only breach. The unverified toast uses a copy of D6.3.a with `verified: false` to exercise the badge; the real record is verified. The two speeding toasts are one episode (`speeding-0`, then `escalated`), so the finished report holds it once at its worst tier. `headingRad` is 0, so `nav.bearingRad` reads as relative in previews. `withToasts` has `speedLimitVerified: false`, and the escalated speeding breach (also in the report) has `basisVerified: false`, as when the limit is an unverified TT 38 default; every other state and breach is verified. Each state carries `controls` (throttle, brakes, steering, handbrake): `ready` has the handbrake on, `running` part throttle, `withToasts` the brake with some left steering. Every state has `controlPreset: real`, `mode: scored` and a `notices` list: empty in `ready` and `running`; from `withToasts` on, one `npc-fault` notice (a red-light motorbike), which the finished report also lists. |

Regenerate `frames-straight.json` after a deliberate change with
`UPDATE_FIXTURES=1 npx vitest run src/testing`. It is parsed JSON, so check it with
`assertFrame(frame, {parsed: true})`.
